identity.title: Position: Generative AI Regulation Can Learn from Social Media Regulation

problem.claim: Generative AI regulation is widely supported, but approaches differ between extending existing laws and creating new ones.

contributions.claim: Argues that evidence from social media regulation can inform generative AI regulation.
Offers four recommendations concerning bias and perceived bias, specific regulatory concerns and trust and safety, computational social science research, and global perspective.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper’s stated contribution is to connect generative AI regulation debates with lessons from social media regulation.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames broad agreement on regulating generative AI alongside disagreement about regulatory approach.
It notes that allegations of political bias against AI companies resemble allegations previously faced by social media companies.
It compares the affordances of generative AI and social media to identify similarities and differences.
It develops four policy recommendations based on the evolution and regulation of social media.
It argues that applying social-media lessons could reduce effort and time and help avoid mistakes in generative AI regulation.

source_observation.claim: The paper moves from comparing the affordances of two technologies to policy recommendations, while preserving both their similarities and differences.

lessons.interpretation: Cross-domain analogy is more useful when paired with an explicit comparison of what carries over and what does not.
lessons.application: Structure a policy position by first mapping shared and distinct affordances, then deriving recommendations tied to the comparison.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the domains lack sufficiently comparable affordances or regulatory histories.

unknowns: The abstract provides no concrete studies, datasets, cases, or outcome measures supporting the claimed benefits of applying social-media lessons.
The abstract does not specify which affordance similarities or differences justify each recommendation.
